why.lede: The work is already hard. Finding one number in a PDF should not be the part that eats your afternoon.
why.claim: onepagers turns recurring document chores into small, focused tools that show the answer and the evidence together.
why.principle1Description: A focused extractor can understand one document family deeply instead of making you configure a platform first.
why.principle2Description: Every useful value should lead back to its source file, page, box, or text region when you need to check it.
why.principle3Description: The job is not done when text appears on screen. It is done when the checked facts can move into the next step.

faq.title: Answers before you upload.
faq.intro: Clear limits, clear sources, and no mystery about what each document tool does.
faq.a1: onepagers is a collection of focused PDF extraction tools. Each one is built for a specific document workflow and keeps extracted facts connected to their source.
faq.q2: What kind of PDF tools are available?
faq.a2: The current tools cover Closing Disclosure PDFs, discovery productions, and K-1 or 1099 tax forms.
faq.q3: What does the Closing Doc Extractor do?
faq.a3: It finds common closing facts such as loan amounts, costs, cash to close, parties, exhibits, and Bates references in Closing Disclosure PDFs.
faq.q4: What does the Discovery Doc Extractor do?
faq.a4: It turns discovery PDFs into dated, named, numbered facts with the source file and page kept beside each result.
faq.q5: What does the K-1 Extractor do?
faq.a5: It reads K-1 and 1099 values, identifies the form layout when supported, and shows the source box, page, confidence, and text used for each field.
faq.a6: Yes, where the individual tool supports it. OCR is used when a page has no usable text layer, and the result identifies when OCR was used.
faq.q7: Can I see where an extracted value came from?
faq.a7: Yes. Results include source details such as the file, page, form box, Bates reference, or highlighted text region, depending on the tool.
faq.a8: They show how strongly the extractor matched a value to the expected field or source text. Treat them as a review signal, not a replacement for checking the document.
faq.q9: Can I correct an extracted value?
faq.a9: The K-1 Extractor lets you edit values in the review screen and download the checked rows as a CSV. The other tools provide their own result exports.
faq.q10: What file types does onepagers accept?
faq.a10: The tools accept PDF files. They do not accept Word documents, images, spreadsheets, or other file types through the upload controls.
faq.q11: How large can my PDF be?
faq.a11: Limits depend on the tool: Closing supports up to 20 MB per PDF and 100 MB per batch; Discovery and K-1 show an 8 MB and 15-page free-processing boundary before heavy work is queued.
faq.q12: How many PDFs can I upload at once?
faq.a12: Closing supports batches of up to 50 PDFs. Discovery supports a batch within its displayed batch limit, while K-1 is designed for one tax-form PDF at a time.
faq.q13: What happens when a file is too large or too long?
faq.a13: The tool accepts the upload and places work beyond the free size or page boundary in the existing heavy-work queue when that path is available. The screen tells you when a file is queued instead of pretending it finished.
faq.q14: Are my documents stored after processing?
faq.a14: Uploaded PDF bytes are automatically deleted after processing. The tools do not keep a document history; only the extracted results and source metadata needed for the current review remain in the active session.
faq.q15: Does onepagers train on my documents?
faq.a15: No. Uploaded documents are not used to train models, and onepagers staff do not have access to processed file contents.
faq.a16: The public experience is the browser upload tool. A public, documented API is not currently advertised.
faq.a17: Accuracy depends on the PDF’s text layer, layout, scan quality, and how closely it matches the supported document type. Always use the source and confidence indicators to review important values.
faq.a18: The current browser tools are available to try without a posted price. Paid processing is described as future work, and no subscription or usage price is currently published.
faq.a19: Yes. Depending on the tool, you can download CSV or JSON results, or a checked CSV from the review screen.
faq.a20: They are for people who repeatedly review closing documents, legal discovery productions, or tax forms and need the facts without losing the source evidence.
